title: Known By Their Actions: Fingerprinting LLM Browser Agents via UI Traces
abstract: arXiv:2605.14786v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As LLM-based agents increasingly browse the web on users' behalf, a natural question arises: can websites passively identify which underlying model powers an agent? Doing so would represent a significant security risk, enabling targeted attacks tailored to known model vulnerabilities. Across 14 frontier LLMs and four web environments spanning information retrieval and shopping tasks, we show that an agent's actions and interaction timings, captured via a passive JavaScript tracker, are sufficient to identify the underlying model with up to 96\% F1 within a fixed harness. Although fingerprints are harness-specific, with cross-harness transfer falling to near chance, pooling traces across harnesses recovers model identification at 0.74 to 0.81 Macro-F1. We further show that strong classifiers can be trained from roughly one third of the available traces, and that identification improves steadily as more events are observed. Injec

translated_title: 观其行而知其名：通过UI轨迹对LLM浏览器代理进行指纹识别
translated_abstract: 随着基于LLM的代理越来越多地代表用户浏览网页，一个自然的问题随之而来：网站能否被动地识别出驱动代理的底层模型？如果能，这将构成重大安全风险，使针对已知模型漏洞的定向攻击成为可能。在14个前沿LLM和四个涵盖信息检索与购物任务的Web环境中，我们展示了通过被动JavaScript追踪器捕获的代理行为和交互时间，足以在固定测试框架内以高达96%的F1分数识别底层模型。尽管指纹具有框架特定性——跨框架迁移时识别效果降至接近随机水平——但汇集跨框架的轨迹仍能以0.74至0.81的Macro-F1恢复模型识别能力。我们进一步表明，仅用约三分之一的可用轨迹即可训练出强大的分类器，并且随着观察到的事件数量增加，识别性能会稳步提升。
tldr: 研究表明网站可通过被动JavaScript追踪器捕获LLM浏览器代理的UI操作轨迹与交互时间，以高达96%的F1分数识别其底层模型，从而带来被定向攻击的安全风险。
